description.en: Monthly pension-amount threshold (EUR 1,000/month) separating 'small' from other pensions for a special banded revalorization rule, used in the Comp_Cond parameter of uprate_bands_es's BenCalc function, commented 'Backrating from 2013 to 2012 (in bands)' -- i.e. applied when converting monetary values between the 2012 and 2013 policy years to decide which uprating index applies to a given pension. It works together with sibling constants defined in the same policy, $uprate_bands_2013A_index (1.02) and $uprate_bands_2013B_index (1.01), reproducing Spain's differentiated 2013 pension revalorization: a 2% increase for pensions up to this EUR 1,000/month threshold and a 1% increase for pensions above it, introduced as part of austerity-era social security legislation.

label.en: Index used for the calculation of social benefits (IPREM) - monthly

description.en: IPREM (Indicador Público de Renta de Efectos Múltiples) is Spain's official multi-purpose reference index for social-benefit eligibility thresholds and amounts, which replaced the minimum wage in this role in 2004; it is stored as a monthly value (600 EUR at the latest of 10 recorded observations since 2005-01-01). It is the most widely referenced constant in this batch, used across 13 sites: it sets ceilings, floors and eligibility tests in several bsarg_es regional minimum-income schemes (e.g. Castilla y León's benefit ceiling, Galicia's minimum cap, La Rioja's income/age eligibility check), drives the income-tiered payment rates of Andalucía's means-tested child benefit bchrg_es (120%/110%/100%/50% of the basic amount for family income up to 1/2/4/6 times IPREM), sets the large-family definition in bch00_es and the parental-benefit amount in bmanc_es, and fixes the statutory floor and ceiling of the contributory unemployment benefits bunct_es and bunct02_es (e.g. a floor of 80% of monthly IPREM, or 107% with a dependent child, and ceilings of 175%-225%, each increased by one sixth).

description.en: IRSC (Indicador de Renda de Suficiència de Catalunya) is Cataluña's own income-sufficiency reference index, used instead of the national IPREM to size the region's minimum-income scheme; it is stored monthly (801.85 EUR at the latest of 10 recorded values since 2005-01-01). It is used once in bsarg_es's BenCalc as the Comp_perTU parameter for '51 - Catalunya: GMI amount', i.e. directly to compute the Renda Garantida de Ciutadania entitlement. Per the country report, the basic benefit equals 100% of IRSC for a one-member household and 150% for two members (with 100 EUR added per further member via $bsarg_rg51_extra_amt), and the overall entitlement is bounded between 10% and 182% of IRSC.

label.en: Parameter to switch between inverted wages and imputed wages (estimated in do-file 13b); 1 - use imputed wages; 0 - use inverted wages

description.en: Binary switch (0 = inverted wages [current value], 1 = imputed wages) defined in the general constants policy (ConstDef_es) that selects how EUROMOD reconstructs a claimant's prior contribution base for the contributory unemployment benefit. It feeds the Comp_Cond parameter of a component in bunct_es/BenCalc ('Previous contribution base'), i.e. it acts as a condition switch selecting which method is used to compute that base. Per the Country Report's EUROMOD modelling note, because contribution history is not observed in EU-SILC, the benefit's underlying contributory base is simulated either by imputing wages (via a separate Stata estimation, do-file 13b, referenced in the constant's own label) or, at the current setting (0), by reversing/inverting the benefit's own calculation rules from observed benefit receipt.

description.en: SMI2 is a technical variant of the national minimum wage (Salario Mínimo Interprofesional) that the model freezes at its 2018 monthly level (735.90 EUR at the latest of 12 recorded values since 2005-01-01), used to index certain regional minimum-income rules that reference 'the minimum wage' as a benefit ceiling without automatically following its later increases. It is used in bsarg_es for Aragón's benefit ceiling (ArithOp UpLim, '24 - Aragón: Benefit amount' — consistent with the pre-2022 Ingreso Aragonés de Inserción being capped at the minimum wage) and for the Basque Country's lone-parent complement (BenCalc Comp_perTU, matching the country report's '6.4% additional amount of the minimum wage' for lone-parent households). It also appears in the historical DefConst formula for Madrid's GMI upper limit ($bsarg_rg30_up_lim), whose current formula instead references the live $SMI.

label.en: Qualifying period for SE: over last

description.en: Represents the length, in months, of the look-back reference period over which a self-employed person's months of activity are counted to test the minimum-contribution requirement for Spain's self-employed unemployment/cessation-of-activity benefit (bunct02_es, "prestación por cese de actividad de trabajadores autónomos"). Defined once in the country-wide ConstDef_es policy, it is used as the uplim parameter of the BenCalc function in bunct02_es that accumulates a claimant's qualifying months of self-employed activity (output liwmy02_s), capping the count at $UBSE_QperTot; the subsequent Elig function then requires this capped count to reach at least $UBSE_QperMin (12 months) for entitlement. This implements the Country Report's rule that self-employed workers need at least 12 consecutive months of contribution to the cese-de-actividad protection during the 2 years immediately preceding unemployment; in the model the constant is "n/a" before 2011 (the scheme did not yet exist) and has held steady at 24 months in every system year from 2011, when the scheme entered the model, onward.

description.en: $bsa00_BCA_rate is the technical initialization value (fixed at 1, marked "DO NOT CHANGE" in the modeller comment) for the Benefit Calibration Adjustment (BCA) rate used by Spain's nation-wide minimum income scheme (Ingreso Mínimo Vital, bsa00_es). It is defined generically in ConstDef_es and consumed inside bsa00_es's own DefConst function as an input feeding $bsa00_rate, where it is combined via a minimum operation with the benefit take-up-adjustment rate ($bsa00_BTA_rate) so that, when both the BTA and BCA extensions are switched on, the lower of the two rates is the one applied to the simulated benefit. Per the ES country report, when the BCA extension is active the true calibration rate is computed automatically by EUROMOD from the aggregate IMV expenditure entered in the External Statistics table (data available for 2020-2023, with the 2023 rate reused for 2024); the fixed value of 1 recorded here is therefore only the neutral default/placeholder that applies before or absent that calibration, consistent with the instruction not to edit it directly.

label.en: Engineers and those with a university degree (Ingenieros y licenciados), Aged 18+ and With tertiary education, and Occupation: 1 Senior officials and managers, or 2 Professionals

description.en: Minimum monthly contribution base for contributory group 1 (the highest-skill group) of the Agrarian Special System — workers aged 18+ with tertiary education in senior-official/managerial or professional occupations ('Ingenieros y licenciados'). The government fixes minimum (and maximum) contributory bases annually by professional category (Country Report Table 2.50); an employee's actual contribution base is the greater of their wage and this category floor. Used in tscag_es/BenCalc (Comp_perTU, 'Contribution base') to compute the base on which agrarian-regime social contributions are levied. At 1,989.30 EUR/month it is about 3.1% above the 2025 Country Report figure (1,929.00), consistent with the base's annual uprating.

description.en: This constant is the maximum monthly Social Security contribution base (tope máximo de cotización) applied under Spain's General Regime, a ceiling fixed annually by the government (Country Report Table 2.49 shows it rising from EUR 4,139.40/month in 2022 to EUR 4,909.50/month in 2025); the model tracks it from 2005 onward, with a latest value of EUR 5,101.20/month. It is defined once in ConstDef_es and reused across several policies as an upper limit on contribution-related amounts: in tscft_es/BenCalc (param uplim) it directly caps the wage base subject to employees' Social Security contributions. It also caps the 'previous contribution base' used to compute two earnings-replacement benefits described in the related Country Report sections: bmact_es/BenCalc and bpact_es/BenCalc (param Comp_UpLim) apply it when deriving the regulatory base (BR) for the parental leave/birth-and-care-of-child benefit, whose amount equals 100% of BR based on the contribution base of the month before the leave starts, and bunct_es/BenCalc (param #_UpLim) applies it to the average daily contributory base underlying the contributory unemployment benefit (paid at 70% of that base for the first 180 days, then 50-60% thereafter). Finally, the LMA labour-market-alignment add-on reuses it in LMA_INIT/BenCalc (param UpLim) to cap the previous contribution base assigned to individuals it newly simulates as unemployed.

description.en: This constant sets the contribution rate for work-related injury and occupational-sickness cover ('accidentes de trabajo y enfermedad', accidents at work and occupational illness) within the Agrarian Self-Employed Special Regime, expressed as a proportion (0.01 = 1%) of the contribution base. It is used in the tscseag_es policy's ArithOp function (func_comment: 'Contribution: accidents and sickness (Acc Trabajo y Enfermedad)') to compute this component of the self-employed farmer's social-security bill. The Country Report's Table 2.59 (Contributory rates, Agrarian Self-employed Special Regime) lists a 1% rate for 'Other protection (work accidents and professional sickness)', payable when the self-employed farmer does not separately contribute to full work-related injury insurance; per the report, this and related covers (occupational training insurance, protection due to termination of activity) became compulsory for the self-employed from 2019 onward. The constant carries a single value across its whole time series (from 2005), i.e. it is modelled as unchanged at 1% throughout.

description.en: This constant is the contribution rate to the Intergenerational Equity Mechanism (Mecanismo de Equidad Intergeneracional, MEI) paid by self-employed farmers under the Agrarian Self-Employed Special Regime, expressed as a proportion of the contribution base. It feeds the Formula of the tscseag_es policy's ArithOp function (func_comment: 'Contribution: IEM (mecanismo de equidad intergeneracional)'), which computes this contribution component. The Country Report's Table 2.59 documents the MEI rate for this regime as introduced in 2023 at 0.6% and rising by 0.1 percentage point each year (0.7% in 2024, 0.8% in 2025); the constant's latest modelled value, 0.9% (0.009), continues that legislated annual step-up beyond the years shown in the report. The constant takes 5 distinct values over its 2005-onward time series, consistent with a nil/undefined rate before MEI's 2023 introduction followed by the successive yearly increases.

description.en: This constant sets a contribution rate for pension insurance ('contingencias comunes') within the Agrarian Self-Employed Special Regime, expressed as a proportion (0.265 = 26.5%) of the contribution base. It is used as the Comp_perTU component of the tscseag_es policy's BenCalc function (func_comment: 'Contribution: pensions (contingencias comunes) from 2012 on'), i.e. added once per tax unit to the pension-contribution amount, applicable to systems from 2012 onward. The Country Report's Table 2.59 lists a pension-insurance contributory rate of 26.50% for the Agrarian regime, unchanged across 2022-2025; the regime also applies a reduced 18.75% rate when the monthly contribution base is below a specified threshold ('amount monthly contributory base exceeding'), so this constant - labelled 'rate2 (basic)' - most likely represents the general/higher-band rate rather than that reduced-base rate. It holds 2 distinct values across its full 2005-onward time series, consistent with a different rate having applied before the 2012 change referenced in the usage comment.

description.en: Sets the number of months of Spain's self-employed "cese de actividad" unemployment-insurance entitlement (bunct02_es) awarded to claimants whose accumulated contribution period falls in the lowest bracket — between 12 and 17 months — with no age distinction (the same value applies whether the claimant is under or over 60). It is the Comp_perTU value used in two components (dag<60 and dag>=60) of the 7th BenCalc in bunct02_es, whose selected duration (bunctmy02_s) is later divided by 12 to pro-rate the annual benefit amount into the monthly payment (bunct02_s = i_bunct02 * bunctmy02_s / 12). In the model it was 2 months when the scheme was first simulated (2011-2018) and was raised to 4 months from system year 2019 onward, matching the Country Report's Table 2.5, which shows 4 months of benefit duration for 12-17 months of contribution (2024 values).

description.en: Benefit-amount rate, expressed as a share of IPREM (Spain's public multi-purpose income indicator; unit '/1'), defined in policy bunmt_es and used directly inside the Formula of its ArithOp function (commented 'Amount') that computes the cash benefit. Its value history is 'n/a' before 2009, 0.80 (80% of IPREM) in 2009-2010, then 0.75 (75% of IPREM) from 2011 to date. Its used_count of 8, double the 4 seen for the national rate constants, suggests the same threshold is also reused as a Band_UpLim in the parallel regional 'cuota D' schedule, since Spain applies the state and regional savings-tax components over identical income bands. label.en: Family Tax Allowance (Minimo Familiar): amount for 1st child

description.en: Annual allowance amount attributable to a taxpayer's first dependent child within Spain's national child tax allowance ('mínimo por descendientes', part of the Mínimo Familiar) under the IRPF. It is the Comp_perTU value of one component group in the BenCalc computing the national Family Tax Allowance in tinit_es (site comment 'National Family Tax Allowance for Children (Mínimo Familiar por Hijos)'); per BenCalc's mechanics a Comp_perTU amount is added once to the result when that component's condition (presumably keyed to having at least one dependent child) is met, reducing the tax base rather than being paid as cash. The allowance rises with each further child through sibling constants $tin_childall_amt2 (2,700 €, 2nd), $tin_childall_amt3 (4,000 €, 3rd) and $tin_childall_amt4 (4,500 €, 4th and following), plus the $tin_childall_amt5 supplement for children under 3. Latest value 2,400 €/year, with 4 recorded values since 2005-01-01.

label.en: C. Cantabria_ Family Tax Allowance (Minimo Familiar): amount for 3rd child

description.en: $tin_childallrg13_amt3 holds Cantabria's region-specific amount of the 'mínimo por descendientes' (dependent-children personal/family tax credit) for a taxpayer's 3rd child, applied under the regional ('autonómico') tranche of Spain's personal income tax (IRPF) in place of the State amount. It is defined in tin_cons_es and consumed by tinit_es's BenCalc function via the Comp_perTU parameter of a component commented 'Regional Family Tax Allowance for Children (Mínimo Familiar por Hijos)'; tinit_es is EUROMOD's individual-taxation IRPF policy (paired with the joint-taxation policy tinjt_es in the same policy family). The Spain country report's 'Personal and family tax credits' section (Table 2.79) confirms Andalucía, Illes Balears, Canarias, Cataluña, Comunidad de Madrid, Galicia, La Rioja and Comunidad Valenciana as the only regions that have legislated their own dependent-children ('mínimo por descendientes') amounts for the regional share of IRPF, replacing the State schedule (EUR 2,400 / 2,700 / 4,000 / 4,500 for the 1st-4th+ child, plus a EUR 2,800 supplement for a child under 3) for those tiers where they diverge; it also states that for any region/tier without its own listed figure 'the corresponding amount in place equals that of the State'. Cantabria is not among the regions listed there, and this constant's recorded value is 'n/a' (State default for a 3rd child: EUR 4,000/year), consistent with Cantabria not having legislated its own 3rd-child amount; the constant appears to exist in tin_cons_es as a structural placeholder mirroring the naming scheme used for regions that do differentiate.

description.en: $tin_childallrg61_amt2 holds Andalucía's region-specific amount of the 'mínimo por descendientes' (dependent-children personal/family tax credit) for a taxpayer's 2nd child, applied under the regional ('autonómico') tranche of Spain's personal income tax (IRPF) in place of the State amount. It is defined in tin_cons_es and consumed by tinit_es's BenCalc function via the Comp_perTU parameter of a component commented 'Regional Family Tax Allowance for Children (Mínimo Familiar por Hijos)'; tinit_es is EUROMOD's individual-taxation IRPF policy (paired with the joint-taxation policy tinjt_es in the same policy family). The Spain country report's 'Personal and family tax credits' section (Table 2.79) confirms Andalucía, Illes Balears, Canarias, Cataluña, Comunidad de Madrid, Galicia, La Rioja and Comunidad Valenciana as the only regions that have legislated their own dependent-children ('mínimo por descendientes') amounts for the regional share of IRPF, replacing the State schedule (EUR 2,400 / 2,700 / 4,000 / 4,500 for the 1st-4th+ child, plus a EUR 2,800 supplement for a child under 3) for those tiers where they diverge; it also states that for any region/tier without its own listed figure 'the corresponding amount in place equals that of the State'. Per Table 2.79, Andalucía's 2nd-child amount has been a stable EUR 2,820/year throughout 2022-2025 (versus the State's EUR 2,700/year), matching this constant's current value exactly.

label.en: Family Tax Allowance (Minimo Familiar): amount per dependent parent

description.en: Represents the national 'mínimo por ascendientes' (allowance for dependent ascendants) component of the Spanish personal income tax (IRPF): the annual tax-free amount attributed for each dependent parent/ascendant (aged 65+, or disabled at any age) who lives with and depends on the taxpayer. In the spine it is wired into the Comp_perElig parameter of the BenCalc components computing tinit_es (individual IRPF) and tinjt_es (joint IRPF), so under BenCalc's semantics it is added once for every eligible dependent parent in the tax unit rather than once per unit. Latest value is EUR 1,150/year per qualifying dependent parent, with 4 distinct values recorded since 2005; it forms the base tier, topped up by $tin_depall_amt2 for parents aged over 75.

description.en: Companion constant to $tin_depall_amt1: the additional national 'mínimo por ascendientes' amount added, per eligible dependent parent, once that parent is aged over 75, on top of the base allowance. Used identically to amt1 - via Comp_perElig in the BenCalc components of tinit_es and tinjt_es for the 'National/Family Tax Allowance for Dependent Parents (Mínimo Familiar por Ascendiente)' - so it is summed once for each qualifying elderly ascendant in the household. Latest value is EUR 1,400/year, giving a combined allowance of EUR 2,550/year for a dependent parent aged over 75 once stacked on the EUR 1,150 base.

label.en: Family Tax Allowance (Minimo Familiar): dependent income limit

description.en: Annual income limit used to determine whether a dependent child counts toward the Family Tax Allowance ('Minimo Familiar'/Minimo por descendientes) in Spain's IRPF. It is used as the DepChildCond parameter of the DefTu function in tinit_es (defining tax unit tu_tinfait) and tinjt_es (tu_tinfajt), i.e. it helps build the tax unit by testing which children qualify as dependents. The Country Report repeatedly applies the same 8,000 euro (excluding exempt income) threshold as the standard definition of a dependent's income limit across several Spanish tax and benefit rules, consistent with this being the corresponding IRPF dependent-child income test.

description.en: Taper (withdrawal) multiplier for Spain's main-residence rent tax credit, applied to the portion of a taxpayer's tax base between $tin_renttc_lim1 (17,707.20 euro) and $tin_renttc_lim2 (24,107.20 euro). Used as the comp_perTu parameter of BenCalc in tinit_es and tinjt_es, it implements the Country Report's formula for the credit in this income band: the maximum credit of $tin_renttc_maxamt (9,040 euro) is reduced by 1.4125 times the excess of the tax base over 17,707.20 euro, reaching zero at 24,107.20 euro. As with the related rent-credit parameters, the credit only applies to pre-2015 contracts and is switched off in the model from 2022.

description.en: Upper bound of the ninth income band in the regional ('autonómica') income-tax scale that Cantabria sets for its own residents within Spain's dual-tier personal income tax (IRPF). It is fixed at an effectively unlimited amount and has held this single value since 2005-01-01; combined with the fact that Cantabria's own rate-9 and rate-10 constants are 0%, this shows bands 6-10 are inert placeholders padding the model's generic 10-band schedule template up to Cantabria's actual, smaller number of live brackets. Inside tin_cons_es an ArithOp formula (function comment v_tin_ts_lt9_rg) multiplies this constant by the region dummy i_reg_13 and sums it with the equivalent 'limit 9' constants of every other Spanish region, so only Cantabria residents receive this value; the selected variable then supplies a Band_UpLim to the SchedCalc 'Regional tax schedule on general income (cuota 2 general autonómica)' in tinit_es/tinjt_es, which computes the regional share of IRPF due on the general taxable base alongside the separately-modelled, uniform nationwide state schedule.

description.en: Marginal tax rate on the first (lowest) income band of the Basque Country's own income-tax scale within Spain's personal income tax (IRPF): currently 9.5%, applying to income up to the EUR 12,450/year threshold held in the sibling constant $tin_rg21_upthres1, and revised four times since 2005-01-01. In tin_cons_es an ArithOp formula (comment v_tin_ts_rt1_rg) multiplies this constant by the region dummy i_reg_21 (the model's Basque Country indicator, built from Guipúzcoa/Vizcaya cases in the data) and adds the equivalent rate-1 constants of every other Spanish region, so only Basque-resident taxpayers receive this rate. The resulting variable feeds Band_Rate 1 of the SchedCalc 'Regional tax schedule on general income (cuota 2 general autonómica)' in tinit_es and tinjt_es — the regional leg of the dual-scale IRPF, computed alongside a separately-modelled uniform state schedule; the Basque Country holds special 'foral' fiscal autonomy over its own taxation under its Economic Agreement (Concierto Económico) with the Spanish state.

description.en: $bsa00_amt is the annual "basic amount" of Spain's nation-wide minimum income scheme (Ingreso Mínimo Vital, IMV), defined directly within bsa00_es and set equal to 100% of the yearly non-contributory pension amount fixed each year by the government; it is the guaranteed-income reference for a single-person family unit. It feeds the Comp_perTU parameter of bsa00_es's BenCalc function (commented "GMI amount"), forming the base figure from which the guaranteed minimum income for the whole family unit is built, increasing by 30% for each additional member up to a ceiling, per the country report. According to the ES country report's Table 2.29, this basic amount rose from EUR 6,563.31 in 2021 to EUR 6,784.44 (2023), EUR 7,250.60 (2024) and EUR 7,905.72 (2025); the model's latest recorded value is EUR 8,803.20 per year, reflecting further annual uprating beyond the years shown in that table. The scheme was established by Real Decreto-ley 20/2020 (consolidated in Ley 19/2021, de 20 de diciembre, por la que se establece el ingreso mínimo vital).

description.en: $bsa00_lim is the "basic wealth" constant of Spain's nation-wide minimum income scheme (Ingreso Mínimo Vital), representing the baseline net-wealth ceiling (financial and property assets other than the main residence) used in the scheme's wealth test for a single-person family unit; its raw definition, "8803.20#y*3", is three times the current annual basic amount ($bsa00_amt). It is used in bsa00_es's BenCalc function via the Comp_perTU parameter (commented "Asset conditions"), supplying the wealth-test threshold applied when calculating entitlement. Per the ES country report, the maximum net wealth for a single-person unit is 3 times the basic amount, increasing by 40% for each additional family member up to a ceiling described in the report's text as 220% of the basic amount (300% if the unit includes children under 18), though the report's own summary table states a 260% cap; this constant supplies only the single-member base figure, with the family-size scaling and ceiling applied elsewhere in the policy. Historically this base wealth limit rose in step with the basic amount, from about EUR 19,689.92 (3x the 2021 basic amount per Table 2.29) to EUR 23,717.16 (3x the 2025 basic amount).

description.en: Upper limit of the seventh and last finite band (10,695,996.06 EUR) in the progressive schedule that the twl_es policy applies, via SchedCalc's Band_UpLim parameter, to a taxpayer's taxable net wealth to compute Spain's Net Wealth Tax (Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio) liability; the band runs from the sixth bracket's limit ($twl_bracket6) up to this value and is taxed at $twl_rate7, while an eighth, unbounded band above this threshold is taxed at the schedule's top marginal rate ($twl_rate8). This value matches Spain's general state-level wealth-tax scale (the default schedule in regions without their own). The country report classifies this tax as included in the micro-data but not actively simulated in the standard EUROMOD run, due to limited wealth data in the underlying survey.

description.en: General, state-level minimum exempt amount (700,000 EUR) of net wealth under Spain's Net Wealth Tax (Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio). It is used in the twl_es policy's ArithOp Formula to reduce a taxpayer's net worldwide wealth before the remaining taxable base is run through the progressive band schedule implemented via SchedCalc ($twl_bracket1-7 and $twl_rate1-8). Per the country report, wealth below this threshold is untaxed and a higher exempt amount applies when the asset is the taxpayer's main residence; because the tax is fully devolved to Spain's regions, some apply a different exempt minimum or near-total relief (the report cites the Comunidad de Madrid granting a 100% tax credit on the final liability). As with the rest of twl_es, the report classifies the tax as included in the micro-data but not actively simulated in the standard EUROMOD run.

description.en: Marginal rate (0.2%) applied, via SchedCalc's Band_Rate parameter in the twl_es policy, to the portion of a taxpayer's net-wealth taxable base falling in the first band of Spain's Net Wealth Tax (Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio) schedule - wealth up to $twl_bracket1 (167,129.45 EUR), after the general exempt amount ($twl_exemption) has been deducted. It is the lowest of eight marginal rates ($twl_rate1-8, rising to 2.5% on wealth above the top threshold) that together make the tax progressive. description.en: Represents the standard monthly fee for the childcare 'dining service' (comedor) modelled by Spain's childcare-cost policy xcc_es. In xcc_es/BenCalc's 'Costs - Dining Fee' component (Comp_perElig, condition commented 'standard dining fee from 0 to 2'), it is added once for every household member aged 0-2 recorded as being in formal (paid) childcare (input flag dccfc=1), building the gross output variable xcc_s, i.e. the pre-discount childcare/dining cost. Fixed at EUR 96/month since the policy was introduced into the model in 2024, it is the base amount the means-tested 'Becas Comedor' discounts ($xccdc_amt1-3) are set against in the companion 'Deductions' component of the same policy.

classification.reason: Childcare cost amount; #m raw_value confirms monthly

description.en: An annual means-tested discount on the childcare dining-fee cost, paid through Spain's 'Becas Comedor' (dining-service grant) mechanism inside the xcc_es childcare-cost policy. It is the Comp_perElig amount of the broader eligibility band of xcc_es/BenCalc's 'Deductions (Becas Comedor)' component, which the model's own comment describes as the 'discount per school year for families receiving the IMV [Ingreso Minimo Vital] with household income ranging from EUR 3,000 to EUR 8,400, or for families with a household income below EUR 8,400' (income tested against ils_origy, original income), for a household member aged 0-2 in formal childcare. It has held at EUR 445 per eligible child per year since the policy's introduction in 2024.

classification.reason: Childcare discount amount; #y raw_value confirms yearly

description.en: An annual means-tested discount under the same 'Becas Comedor' dining-fee mechanism in xcc_es, but for its most generous, lowest-income band. The model's own comment on this xcc_es/BenCalc 'Deductions (Becas Comedor)' component (Comp_perElig) describes it as the 'discount per school year for families receiving the Social Assistance (Ingreso Minimo Vital) with a household income below EUR 3,000' — i.e. it applies to Ingreso-Minimo-Vital-recipient households (bsa00_s>0) with original income (ils_origy) at or below $xccdc_lim1 and a child aged 0-2 in formal care. Live inspection of the model shows the amount rising from EUR 800/year in the 2024 system to EUR 979/year from 2025 onward, its current value and the largest of the module's three per-child discounts.

classification.reason: Childcare discount amount; #y raw_value confirms yearly

description.en: An annual discount specific to large families ('familia numerosa', flagged in the model by dlg_s=1) under the 'Becas Comedor' dining-fee mechanism in xcc_es. It is the Comp_perElig amount of a third component in xcc_es/BenCalc's 'Deductions (Becas Comedor)' function, documented in the model as the 'discount for large families with a household income between EUR 8,400 and EUR 10,000' — for a large family's child aged 0-2 in formal care whose household original income (ils_origy) falls between $xccdc_lim2 and $xccdc_lim3, a band that gives no discount to other households. It is not modelled (value 'n/a') before 2026 and takes its first value, EUR 295/year, only from the 2026 system, matching the '2026 reform' flagged on the paired threshold $xccdc_lim3.

classification.reason: Large family discount; #y raw_value confirms yearly

label.en: Income Limit 1: Deduction to childcare cost

description.en: The lowest of three annual household-income ceilings (tested against ils_origy, EUROMOD's original-income concept) structuring the means test for the 'Becas Comedor' dining-fee discount in xcc_es. Within xcc_es/BenCalc's 'Deductions (Becas Comedor)' function it is used in the Comp_Cond condition that separates the most generous discount band ($xccdc_amt2 = EUR 979/year, for Ingreso-Minimo-Vital-recipient households at or below this limit) from the broader band ($xccdc_amt1 = EUR 445/year, covering IMV recipients between this limit and $xccdc_lim2, plus non-IMV households below $xccdc_lim2). It has been fixed at EUR 3,000/year since the policy's introduction in 2024.

classification.reason: Income eligibility limit; #y raw_value confirms yearly

label.en: Income Limit 2: Deduction to childcare cost

description.en: The second of three annual household-income ceilings (ils_origy) in the means test for the 'Becas Comedor' dining-fee discount in xcc_es. In xcc_es/BenCalc's 'Deductions (Becas Comedor)' function it is the Comp_Cond upper bound of the broader EUR 445/year discount band ($xccdc_amt1) — covering both Ingreso-Minimo-Vital recipients and non-recipients with a child aged 0-2 in formal care — and it also forms the lower boundary of the large-family band gated by $xccdc_lim3. It has been fixed at EUR 8,400/year since 2024.

classification.reason: Income eligibility limit; #y raw_value confirms yearly

label.en: Income Limit 3: Deduction to childcare cost. 2026 reform

description.en: The upper income ceiling (tested against ils_origy) of a large-family-only band added to the 'Becas Comedor' dining-fee deduction in xcc_es/BenCalc's 'Deductions (Becas Comedor)' function. Paired with $xccdc_lim2 in that component's Comp_Cond, it brackets the EUR 8,400-10,000/year income range within which a large family (dlg_s=1) with a child aged 0-2 in formal care receives the EUR 295/year discount ($xccdc_amt3), extending eligibility beyond the EUR 8,400 ceiling that applies to other households. As its own label states, this is a '2026 reform': live inspection of the model confirms the constant is not modelled (n/a) in 2024-2025 and takes its EUR 10,000/year value only from the 2026 system, alongside the newly introduced $xccdc_amt3.

classification.reason: Income limit for 2026 reform; #y confirms yearly
